s0DEC33.name: Draw Yoshi's house, switch palace edge
summary: Two level object draw routines. $0DEC33 (Yoshi's house): writes a fixed 16x10 block of Map16 tiles from DATA_0DEB93 (row by row, page 0).
$0DEC5C (switch palace right/bottom edge): writes the single Map16 tile $110 (page 1).
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DEC66.name: Table: water weed Map16 tiles
summary: Top and bottom tile ($0C9, $0CA). Quirk: the disassembly's data was once mis-decoded as CMP #$CA.

s0DEC68.name: Draw water weed object
summary: Writes a 1x2 stack of tiles from DATA_0DEC66 (page 0), moving down a row after each.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DEC7E.name: Table: switch Map16 tiles
summary: Four switches (green, yellow, blue, red), 4 tiles each: top row left/right, then bottom row left/right (Map16 $0EC-$0FB, page 0).

s0DEC8E.name: Draw switch palace switch, ghost house window
summary: $0DEC8E: draws the 2x2 switch for color X = object number - $8A, unless the matching switch palace flag [$1F27+X] is already set.
$0DECC1 (ghost house window): sets X = 8 and jumps into the ghost house cobweb code at $0DE9F5, which draws the 2x2 window tiles $0FC-$0FF.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DECC6.name: Table: background block Map16 tiles
summary: Indexed by type: $092 grey bricks background, $15E wooden block (page 1 via the CPX #1 check), $082 log background.

s0DECC9.name: Draw grey bricks, wooden blocks, log bg
summary: Fills a (width+1) x (height+1) rectangle with one Map16 tile chosen by type X = object number - $34 (also entered at $0DECCE from the log background object with X = 2).
Type 1 (wooden blocks) writes on Map16 page 1, the others on page 0.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DED09.name: Table: log and hand rail Map16 tiles
summary: Three 3-byte rows (left, middle, right tile) each indexed by type 0-2: $082 log background, $089/$08A/$08B hand rail, $088.

s0DED12.name: Draw horizontal log bg, wood ledge
summary: $0DED12: one row of tiles, left + (width) middle + right, taken from the tables at DATA_0DED09 by type (high nibble).
$0DED43 (wood ledge without column): one row, left $10A, middle $10B, right $10C (page 1). $0DED4A is also called by the column ledge routine.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DED65.name: Table: vertical log Map16 tiles
summary: Top tile and middle tile by type: $083/$078/$079 and $083/$079/$079 (page 0).

s0DED6B.name: Draw vertical log background
summary: Writes a vertical column of (height+1) tiles: the top tile and then middle tiles from the type tables DATA_0DED65/DATA_0DED68.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DED95.name: Table: vertical edge Map16 tiles
summary: One tile per type ($15F, $160, $15A, $15B on page 1) for the solid vertical edge and spike column objects.

s0DED99.name: Draw edges, ledges, cloud, grass ledge 2
summary: Several object routines: vertical brick edges/spike columns ($0DED99), the bonus room wood ledge ($0DEDB9), the four switch palace pieces (upside down ledge $0DEDDB,
ledge $0DEE17, right facing edge $0DEE52, left facing edge $0DEE89), wood ledge on column ($0DEEC0), cloud ledge ($0DEF45) and grass ledge 2 ($0DEF67).
The column ledge draws the ledge row, then (height) tall $078/$079 log columns every 4 tiles beneath it, one column per [$00] + 1.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DEFA2.name: Table: wooden crate Map16 tiles
summary: Interior row tiles: left ($163,$165 page 1), middle ($0C7,$0C8 page 0) and right ($164,$16A page 1); the row used alternates per line.

s0DEFA8.name: Draw wooden crate, grass ledge 1, log bg
summary: $0DEFA8: wooden crate, top row $161/$10D/$162, interior rows alternating between two patterns, bottom row $16B/$16C/$16D (page 1 mostly).
$0DF02B: grass ledge 1, a $10F top row (page 1) over $0EA fill rows. $0DF066: log background, enters the rectangle fill with X = 2.
Quirk: the crate and ledge code uses BNE as an always-taken branch after loading a non-zero tile.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DF06B.name: Table: spike Map16 tile
summary: The single entry $159 (page 1) used by the upward spikes object.

s0DF06C.name: Draw thin upward spikes
summary: Writes a row of (width+1) spike tiles from DATA_0DF06B on page 1. The tile index comes from the high nibble, which only works for 0.
Parameters: [$57]: position in the Map16 buffer, [$59]: size byte (width/height nibbles), [$6B]/[$6E]: Map16 buffer pointers.

s0DF08A.name: Padding: $FF fill
summary: Unused $FF bytes up to the stripe images at $0DF300.

s0DF300.name: Ending stripe image: Lakitu enemies
summary: Stripe image record (read by CODE_00871E): VRAM address high, low, size word (bit 15 vertical, bit 14 RLE fill, low 14 bits = byte count - 1), then data; $FF ends the image.
Ending enemy list screen ('Ending: Enemies: Lakitu' in ImagePointers). RLE records clear BG tilemap areas to tile $FA / property $34 (tile counts are about size / 2);
the text records write 8x8 tile letters with property $38 to the BG3 tilemap at VRAM $5xxx. Text: FISHIN'LAKITU; PARA-BOMB; PARA-GOOMBA; LAKITU; SPINY; WIGGLER; BOB-OMB.

s0DF42D.name: Ending stripe image: Hammer Bro. enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: AMAZING FLYIN'; HAMMER BROTHER; SUPER KOOPA; CHARGIN'; CHUCK; JUMPING; PIRHANA PLANT; VOLCANO; LOTUS.

s0DF572.name: Ending stripe image: Pokey enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: SUMO BROTHER; MONTY MOLE; POKEY; BULLET BILL.

s0DF66B.name: Ending stripe image: Rex enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: REX; MEGA MOLE; BANZAI BILL.

s0DF742.name: Ending stripe image: Dino-Rhino enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: DINO-RHINO; DINO-TORCH; KOOPAS.

s0DF837.name: Ending stripe image: Blargg enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: SPIKE TOP; SWOOPERS; BUZZY BEETLE; BLARGG.

s0DF8FA.name: Ending stripe image: Urchin enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: BLURPS; URCHIN; PORCU-PUFFER; TORPEDO TED; RIP VAN FISH.

s0DF9CD.name: Ending stripe image: Boo enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: "BOO" BUDDIES; FISHIN'BOO; THE BIG "BOO"; EERIES.

s0DFA98.name: Ending stripe image: Dry Bones enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: LIL SPARKY; BONY BEETLE; DRY BONES; THWOMP; THWIMP; HOTHEAD.

s0DFB73.name: Ending stripe image: Grinder enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: GRINDER; BALL'N'CHAIN; FISHBONE.

s0DFC58.name: Ending stripe image: Reznor enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: REZNOR.

s0DFCD5.name: Ending stripe image: Mechakoopa enemies
summary: Same record format as the Lakitu image. Text: MECHAKOOPAS.

s0DFD5C.name: Ending stripe image: Bowser and Koopalings
summary: Ending enemy list screen for Bowser and the Koopalings. One RLE record fills the whole BG tilemap ($2000, 4096 tiles) with $FA/$14, then text records: MORTON; KOOPA JR.; ROY; KOOPA; BOWSER; LEMMY; KOOPA; WENDY; O.KOOPA; IGGY; KOOPA; LARRY; KOOPA; LUDWIG; VON KOOPA.
After the $FF end marker the section continues with three unreferenced text records (PUMPKIN; PIDGIT; MASK KOOPAS) and then $FF padding to the end of the bank.
